plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with a broad umbrella-shaped canopy and fern-like leaves. In the Southern Hemisphere summer it becomes covered in clusters of vivid orange-red flowers, each with one petal streaked with white and yellow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to February); May to July in the Northern Hemisphere tropics
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions including northern Australia, South Africa, Brazil and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: In the wild the species is endangered in Madagascar, yet it is among the most widely planted ornamental trees in the tropics. Its long woody seed pods rattle in the wind.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like blooms. Flowers open in the cool winter months and brighten gardens when little else is flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring (December to March in the Northern Hemisphere, with early cultivars opening in December)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and eastern China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds yield tsubaki oil, which has long been used in Japan for hair and skin care.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing perennial with leathery, dark green, palmate leaves and nodding white cup-shaped flowers that age to a pinkish tone. It flowers in cold weather and can bloom through snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the mountainous woodlands of central and southern Europe, including the Alps and northern Apennines; grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Legend says the flower sprang from the tears of a young girl who had no gift for the Christ child. All parts of the plant are toxic, and it was once used in ancient medicine as a purgative.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like evergreen leaves and tall stalks bearing rounded clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. It thrives in the warm sunny summers of the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February)
plants.location: Native to South Africa's Eastern Cape; naturalized and widely grown in Australia, New Zealand, and coastal California
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily. Its name comes from the Greek words agape (love) and anthos (flower). It has become an invasive weed in parts of Australia and New Zealand.
